newsitem.title: USA: CNS may have new product in early 1998.
newsitem.headline: CNS may have new product in early 1998.

text.p: CNS Inc, which makes and markets a nasal strip used to relieve nasal congestion and snoring, said Thursday it hopes to offer by early next year a product that may be used to suppress appetite or to quit smoking.

CNS has been developing a product, delivered by inhaling, which has shown on a preliminary basis in anecdotal data to suppress appetite and act as an aid in curbing the desire to smoke, CNS President Richard Jahnke told a Piper Jaffray investment conference here.
The active ingredient is a food additive and Jahnke said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration requested safety data on the product.
But before the company funded extensive research to provide the data, it decided to package the active ingredient in a lozenge form and a gum form to test the effectiveness of the product.
"We will be able to determine the efficacy that way," Jahnke said. "That level of efficacy may allow us to market the product that way," he told a Piper Jaffray investment conference here.

The first trials are expected to be conducted this summer with some results available in early fall and, "We will hopefully take the product to market, perhaps with reduced claims, as early as next year," Jahnke said.

CNS' major product is Breathe Right, a nonprescription, nondrug small adhesive strip which, when placed across the bridge of the nose, opens nasal passages and improves breathing. The device is marketed to treat snoring and congestion caused by colds and allergies.

To expand use of the device, CNS is seeking FDA approval to market the product to improve the quality of sleep and to enhance athletic performance. The company has said it hopes these applications for additional claims will be approved before the end of the year.
CNS is also studying the use of the device to treat asthma, emphysema and sleep apnea.
On another front, CNS is introducing a clear version of the strip, which the company said may appeal to some consumers more than the tan-colored product.
It is also developing a version which eliminates some of the adhesive on the strip and is easier to remove.

Jahnke said CNS' agreement with Healthdyne Technologies Inc to market the device to hospitals and nursing homes "will be a slow builder, measured in years not months" but will serve to increase the credibility of the product in the medical arena.
